title: Graph Contrastive Topic Model
read_from: arXiv preprint 2307.02078 (published version: Expert Systems with Applications)
problem: Contrastive neural topic models sample negatives by word frequency, producing false negatives that are semantically similar to the prototype (sample bias).
architecture: GCTM: input document modelled as a document-word bipartite graph (DWBG); positive and negative word co-occurrence graphs encoded by GNNs; document-word information propagation (DWIP) perturbs DWBG edges to generate positive/negative samples; graph contrastive loss combined with the NTM (VAE) loss.
metrics: classification accuracy (Random Forest on document representations)
key_results: NPMI with 50 topics: 20NG 0.379 vs CLNTM+BERT 0.329, IMDB 0.202 vs 0.196, NIPS 0.410 vs 0.396.
NPMI with 200 topics: 20NG 0.338, IMDB 0.184, NIPS 0.387 (best in each case).
Classification accuracy (50 topics): 20NG 0.543 vs CLNTM+BERT 0.525; IMDB 0.874 vs 0.871.
Average prototype-negative similarity 0.108-0.109 for GCTM vs 0.935-0.962 for CLNTM.

strengths.text: Graph-based sampling yields negatives that are semantically far from the prototype, removing the false-negative problem of frequency-based sampling.

limitations.text: Only NPMI is reported for topic quality; no diversity metric.
Performance drops sharply with three GCN layers, and the weight of negative samples needs tuning.
Whether the contrastive loss alone can replace the NTM loss is left for future work.

notes: Queue DOI was the SSRN preprint (10.2139/ssrn.4725374); Crossref gives the ESWA article DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2024.124631, used for citation.
